deep.reconstruction:
This folio holds only small sketches. It continues the previous page, which (a) wrote the p-variable theta series theta(v) = sum_m exp(sum a_{mu mu'} m_mu m_mu' + 2 sum v_mu m_mu) with its quasi-periodicity, (b) introduced real coordinates by v_iota = pi i zeta'_iota + sum_mu zeta_mu a_{iota mu}, and (c) evaluated integrals of d log theta over the boundary of the period cell.

The previous page's integration step, in modern terms: the real 2p-dimensional torus R^{2p}/Z^{2p} carries coordinates (zeta'_1, zeta_1, ..., zeta'_p, zeta_p). Two facts follow from the quasi-periodicity.
- Translation by pi i in v_iota (zeta'_iota -> zeta'_iota + 1) leaves theta unchanged.
- Translation by the iota-th column of a (zeta_iota -> zeta_iota + 1) multiplies theta by exp(-2 v_iota - a_{iota iota}).
So the integral of d log theta around the boundary of the unit square in the (zeta'_iota, zeta_iota) plane equals 2 pi i times an integer: (zeta'_iota, zeta_iota) = 1. Squares in mixed planes give 0, e.g. (zeta'_mu, zeta'_mu') = 0 and (zeta'_1, zeta_2) = 0 (the -2a_{12} + 2a_{12} cancellation).

Riemann then forms products of these elementary pairings over all 2p coordinates. He finds (zeta'_1 zeta_1 zeta'_2 zeta_2) = 2 and (zeta'_1 zeta_1 ... zeta'_3 zeta_3) = 3!. In modern terms, with omega = sum dzeta'_mu ^ dzeta_mu (the first Chern class of the theta line bundle), integral over the torus of omega^p = p!. Equivalently, p generic translates theta(u - e^(1)), ..., theta(u - e^(p)) have p! common zeros. For p = 2 he checks this explicitly with theta(u1 - a1, u2 - a2) and theta(u1 - b1, u2 - b2): the two common zeros alpha, beta are related by the involution u -> a + b - u, with a + gamma = b - delta.

On this page:
(1) Top left, 'lambda1, 2, ... = 2p' (bracketed, with a 2' below). This is most plausibly the enumeration of the real coordinate directions 1, 2, ... (primed and unprimed), 2p in all, i.e. the real dimension of the torus over which the boundary integrals are taken.
(2) Two pairs of overlapping circles joined by a short line. These are best read as a schematic of two translated theta divisors meeting, in the p = 2 picture, in two points. This matches the 'two intersection points' (alpha, beta) count of the previous page. The hatching marks the overlap region.
(3) Three overlapping rectangles with corner labels 1, 2, 1', 2' (and partly blotted 1/2 marks). These depict faces of the period cell spanned by directions 1, 1', 2, 2', glued along shared edges. They are the decomposition used to sum boundary integrals of d log theta over 2-dimensional faces of the 4-dimensional cell.
(4) Two 4x4 arrays of 0/1. Read as rows (zeta'_1, zeta_1, zeta'_2, zeta_2) these appear to record vertices or faces of the unit 4-cube (coordinates 0 or 1), i.e. corners of the period cell used in the bookkeeping. They might alternatively be p = 2 half-period characteristics, since the next page lists 0/1 characteristic arrays. Several entries are blotted, so no definite computation can be extracted.

No equation is derived on this folio itself. It is a diagrammatic aid to the zero-counting computation of the previous page.
